events.title: Kennedy Announces Cuban Missile Crisis Naval Quarantine
events.description: In a televised address, U.S. President John F. Kennedy revealed that the Soviet Union had placed offensive nuclear missiles in Cuba and announced a naval quarantine of the island to prevent further shipments of military equipment.
events.significance: This marked the start of the most dangerous phase of the Cold War, bringing the United States and the Soviet Union to the brink of nuclear war and leading to lasting changes in superpower diplomacy, including the Moscow-Washington hotline.

events.title: Metropolitan Opera Opens in New York City
events.description: The Metropolitan Opera opened its first season with a performance of Gounod's Faust at its original house on Broadway at 39th Street in Manhattan.
events.significance: The Met became one of the world's leading opera companies and a cornerstone of American cultural life, helping establish New York as a global center for the performing arts.

events.title: Chester Carlson Makes the First Xerographic Copy
events.description: Inventor Chester Carlson, with assistant Otto Kornei, produced the first xerographic image in Astoria, Queens, using the inscription '10-22-38 Astoria'.
events.significance: Xerography became the basis for modern photocopying and led to the founding of the Xerox Corporation, transforming how offices and institutions reproduced and shared documents.

events.title: The Great Disappointment
events.description: Followers of the Millerite movement, who believed Jesus Christ would return to Earth on this date as calculated by preacher William Miller, waited in vain and experienced profound disillusionment when nothing happened.
events.significance: The event led to the fragmentation of the Millerites and contributed to the formation of new denominations, including the Seventh-day Adventist Church, shaping American religious history.

events.title: Shah of Iran Admitted to the United States for Medical Treatment
events.description: The deposed Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi was allowed to enter the United States for cancer treatment in New York, despite warnings from some officials about possible backlash in Iran.
events.significance: The decision inflamed anti-American sentiment in Iran and directly led to the seizure of the U.S. Embassy in Tehran on November 4, 1979, triggering the 444-day hostage crisis.
